When the root op finishes, the walk's quiesce_path request is killed from the finisher; the auth's completion ignores the result. On the auth the walk starts before the flag is journaled.
features.notes: Coverage gap: each rank descends only through dirfrags it is auth for, so inodes in a subtree delegated to another rank below a dirfrag of this rank are visited by neither walk; their caps are masked only at their next issue_caps (requests are still gated). Directories with visited children are processed twice (second eval and second MQuarantineDisable). A fully cached tree is typically walked recursively inside one mds_lock hold (inferred).

features.name: Quarantine propagation to replica ranks
features.summary: Carries the quarantine flag to other ranks through ordinary policylock replication and starts a local walk there.
features.description: quarantine_inode xlocks replicated locks, so the auth sends LOCK_AC_LOCK and gathers LOCKACKs (a replica acks only after its local rdlocks on the lock are released); for snaplock and policylock xlocks while the cluster is degraded with a replica rank below active, acquisition waits for full recovery. Releasing the xlock sends LOCK_AC_SYNC with the policylock payload v4, which includes optmetadata; the replica's decode_lock_ipolicy detects a change of has_quarantined on a subvolume root and calls handle_quarantine_policy_update, which starts a local walk whose completion nobody waits for. The auth replies without waiting for replicas, and a replica serves the subvolume normally until it processes LOCK_AC_SYNC.
features.notes: This replaced dedicated MMDSQuarantine messages, EQuarantineStart/Finish/Cancel events and op 0x0150d (commit 24d79f3a038). Requests parked on a replica hold rdlocks on its root snaplock and are woken only by that replica's DEL walk, which needs the auth's xlock, so a disable can wedge until those clients are evicted (inferred, untested).

features.name: Subtree export refused inside a quarantined subvolume
features.summary: Prevents migrating subtrees rooted at or inside a quarantined subvolume.
features.description: Migrator::export_dir silently refuses an export whose root dirfrag's inode is under quarantine (the subvolume root's own dirfrags and every dirfrag inside), also during up:stopping, so balancer exports, export pins and rank shutdown of such subtrees wait until the quarantine is lifted. An export rooted at an ancestor dirfrag (for example /volumes/<group>) is not refused and carries the subvolume root and nested dirfrags along; the persisted flag travels with the inode, the in-memory quarantine_op does not (inferred, untested).
features.notes: QA tear-down disables quarantine and removes export pins before reducing max_mds (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_quarantine.py:1105-1155). See also F-MULTI-025.

features.name: Quarantine re-enforcement after restart
features.summary: Applies the quarantine cap mask again to all reconnected caps when a rank becomes active.
features.description: The persisted flag is restored by replaying the EUpdate metablob or loaded from the parent dirfrag; quarantine_op and the operation registry start empty, and there is no quarantine-specific replay code. MDSRank::active_start calls MDCache::reissue_all_caps, which runs eval and issue_caps for every inode with caps and so applies the quarantine mask to caps that clients reconnected with. Standby-replay daemons replay the same EUpdate. An operation interrupted before its EUpdate was safe leaves the flag unchanged and has to be retried by the administrator.

features.name: Quarantine enforcement predicate
features.summary: Decides for any inode whether it lies inside a quarantined subvolume.
features.description: CInode::is_under_quarantine walks the snaprealm chain from the inode: for each realm's subvolume ino (the outermost enclosing subvolume), if that inode is cached it returns false when a disable is in flight, and true when an enable is in flight or the persisted flag is set; if the subvolume root is not cached it returns false (fail-open); otherwise it continues with the parent realm and returns false at the root realm. Coverage is every inode whose realm chain reaches the root, including snapshot views (.snap) at any depth. It runs on hot paths (every check_access, every Locker::issue_caps, which also builds the inode's full path to check q/Q, every encode_inodestat and loner changes) whether or not anything is quarantined.
features.notes: doc/cephfs/fs-volumes.rst:1620-1622 says an uncached root fails closed; the code fails open (commit 630bf842c11). In practice the root is cached whenever a descendant is. Unlinked-but-open files in stray directories are outside the realm chain and not covered (inferred). Removing ceph.dir.subvolume from a quarantined root silently stops enforcement, and disable returns -EINVAL until the flag is set again.

features.name: MDS auth cap flags q and Q (quarantine access)
features.summary: Quarantine use of the q and Q MDS cap flags.
features.description: See F-ADM-015 for the flags. Quarantine-specific: the flags are consulted in two places, the per-request check for quarantine-aware sessions (F-QOS-071) and the cap restriction on every cap issue (F-QOS-074); neither is implied by allow *, so recovery clients need an explicit q or Q grant.
features.notes: The docs describe q as one quarantined path and Q as all; the code evaluates both identically, scoped by the grant's path and fsname.

features.name: Quarantine client feature bit 24
features.summary: Client feature bit that selects between EACCES enforcement (aware clients) and request parking (unaware clients).
features.description: CEPHFS_FEATURE_QUARANTINE = 24, named "quarantine", is in CEPHFS_FEATURES_ALL, so the MDS and this release's libcephfs, ceph-fuse and NFS-Ganesha advertise it. The Linux kernel client snapshot neither defines nor advertises bit 24 and is always treated as unaware. The bit also decides who receives MQuarantineDisable, and its name is accepted wherever CephFS feature names are, for example fs required_client_features.
features.notes: Older libcephfs, ceph-fuse and Ganesha builds without bit 24 behave like the kernel client (their requests are parked). See also F-PROTO-021 (per-bit gated behaviour).

features.name: EACCES for quarantine-aware sessions
features.summary: Fails every metadata request of a quarantine-aware client without q/Q on an inode under quarantine with -EACCES.
features.description: Server::check_access sets check_qtine when the inode is under quarantine and the session has feature bit 24, and Session::check_access passes it to MDSAuthCaps::is_capable, whose false result becomes -EACCES. check_access runs in essentially every request handler on the target and/or parent inode (with mask 0 for lookups by ino), so all metadata operations of such clients inside the subvolume fail, including snapshot listing and a mount at a path inside it. Batched getattr and lookup followers skip the checks and inherit the batch head's result: success if the head has q, -EACCES (even for a q follower) if the head is an aware client without q, and an indefinite wait if the head is a parked unaware request.
features.notes: The C++ client's readdir tolerates -EACCES from _getattr on a quarantined child and uses cached attributes (commit 630bf842c11); I/O on an already-open file waits for caps instead of failing (code reading). Ganesha maps -EACCES to an NFS access error (inferred, untested). Renaming the subvolume root is gated on its parent: aware clients get -EACCES from check_access on the source inode, unaware clients can rename it (inferred, untested). Batching is enabled by mds_allow_batched_ops (default true). See also F-ADM-018 (per-request access checks).

features.name: Request parking for quarantine-unaware sessions
features.summary: Holds requests of clients without feature bit 24 on a quarantined subvolume inside the MDS, without reply, until the quarantine is lifted.
features.description: Server::check_quarantine_block returns false for internal requests, aware sessions and inodes not under quarantine; otherwise it adds C_MDS_RetryRequest as a WAIT_QUARANTINE waiter on the first quarantined (or being-quarantined) subvolume root up the realm chain and the caller returns without replying. Parking sites: rdlock_path_pin_ref on the target (getattr, lookup, open, readdir, setattr, setlayout, normal setxattr and removexattr, getvxattr, file locks, snapdiff, blockdiff, snapshot metadata), rdlock_path_xlock_dentry on the parent (create, mknod, mkdir, symlink, unlink, rmdir, link by ino), rdlock_two_paths_xlock_destdn on both parents (rename, path-based link) and handle_client_lookup_ino (lookupino, lookuphash, lookupname, lookupparent). Parked requests keep the path locks they already hold (dentry rdlocks, snaplock rdlocks up to /, and for creates parent filelock and nestlock wrlocks plus a dentry xlock) and are woken by the disable walk visiting the root or by an abort; requests woken in the first two sites are not re-checked. Kernel system calls block (killable) without timeout, and a kernel mount inside the subvolume fails with -ETIMEDOUT after mount_timeout (60 s, inferred).
features.notes: Not parked: ceph.* vxattr set/remove and SETDIRLAYOUT addressed by ino, and LOOKUPINO with a snapid; an allow * kernel client can therefore remove ceph.dir.subvolume from a quarantined root (inferred). Held locks can wedge an enable (an unaware request parked between acceptance and the root xlocks holds the root snaplock rdlock, so the command never answers and later ones get -EBUSY) and a disable with replicas; evicting the client unblocks both (inferred, untested). Parked requests are ordinary tracked ops and can raise slow-request warnings.

features.name: Snapshot operation parking under quarantine
features.summary: Parks lssnap, mksnap, rmsnap and renamesnap of unaware clients on quarantined subvolumes.
features.description: handle_client_lssnap, handle_client_mksnap, handle_client_rmsnap and handle_client_renamesnap call check_quarantine_block on the directory and re-run it on every retry, so kernel clients can neither list nor create, remove or rename snapshots (ls, mkdir, rmdir and rename in .snap) of a quarantined subvolume; commit c05f3db248a added this because kernel clients could otherwise destroy recovery snapshots. Snapdir paths are traversed without RDLOCK_PATH or RDLOCK_SNAP, so these parked requests hold no path locks. Aware clients get -EACCES from check_access instead.

features.name: Cap restriction to PIN under quarantine
features.summary: Issues only CEPH_CAP_PIN on inodes under quarantine to sessions without q/Q.
features.description: CInode::get_caps_quarantine_mask returns CEPH_CAP_PIN when the inode is under quarantine and the session lacks quarantine access for its path, and CEPH_CAP_ANY otherwise; the mask is ANDed into the any, loner and xlocker allowed masks, the careful and xlocker masks, get_caps_allowed_for_client, try_drop_loner and the snapped-inode branch of encode_inodestat, and Locker::get_allowed_caps caches the masks per q status. Directories therefore lose Fs, Fx, As, Xs and Ls too. Clients receive ordinary REVOKE messages down to PIN and flush dirty data and metadata as usual: cap flushes and releases are not gated, dentry leases are not restricted, and OSD access is untouched (a client that already holds valid caps or writes objects directly with its OSD caps is not stopped, inferred).
features.notes: Caps issued before a change persist until the next evaluation (walk, lock change, cap request, reissue_all_caps). The cap walk does not proactively revoke caps on the .meta file, but any later issue_caps restricts them.

features.name: EQUARANTINED errno in MClientCaps
features.summary: Tags cap grants and revokes on quarantined inodes with oserrno -1000 for sessions without q/Q.
features.description: MClientCaps HEAD_VERSION 14 appends int32 oserrno after subvolume_id. In Locker::issue_caps, every CEPH_CAP_OP_GRANT or REVOKE built by the main issue/revoke branch for an inode under quarantine carries -EQUARANTINED (EQUARANTINED = 1000) for sessions without q/Q and 0 for sessions with it; the stale-cap re-issue branch, cap import/export and flush acks never set it, and -EQUARANTINED is never a request result. The C++ client marks an inode quarantined on a revoke with -EQUARANTINED and clears the mark on a grant beyond PIN with oserrno 0; the kernel decodes MClientCaps only up to its v12 fields and ignores oserrno.

features.name: QUARANTINE marker in InodeStat
features.summary: Marks the quarantined subvolume root in replies with an optmetadata entry of kind QUARANTINE.
features.description: encode_inodestat adds an optmetadata entry of kind QUARANTINE (2) when the inode itself has the persisted flag (only the subvolume root), with a default quarantine_md_t (enabled true, timestamp 0: the real time is not sent); descendants carry no marker. It is emitted inside InodeStat v9 (sessions with CEPHFS_FEATURE_REPLY_ENCODING) between fscrypt_file and subvolume_id. libcephfs stores optmetadata verbatim and its Inode::is_under_quarantine walks client-side parents for this marker or a -EQUARANTINED cap errno; the kernel skips optmetadata as an opaque versioned blob.

features.name: MQuarantineDisable notification
features.summary: When the quarantine code sends MQuarantineDisable.
features.description: See F-PROTO-097 for the message. Quarantine-specific: on disable the cap-revocation walk sends it to every quarantine-aware session holding a cap on each visited inode, and the QUARANTINE_INODE finisher sends it once more for the root; directories whose walk op had children get it twice. The C++ client's handle_quarantine_disable clears its quarantine mark and signals cap waiters.
features.notes: See also F-QOS-064 (cap-revocation walk), F-QOS-075 (EQUARANTINED errno).
